pl-l4d21c8-d1e115.summary: States that as the penitent must not hide sin, which is pride, so he must not, for humility's sake, confess himself guilty of what he knows he did not commit, since such humility is incautious and makes one a sinner.
claims: Confessing sins not committed is a sin.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e118.summary: Quotes Augustine: when you lie for humility's sake, if you were not a sinner before lying, by lying you become what you avoided; there is no truth in you unless you call yourself a sinner knowing you are one; truth is to say what you are.
claims: Lying out of humility makes one a sinner.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e127.summary: A heading encoded as a paragraph: 'On the punishment of the priest who publishes the sins of one confessing'.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e131.summary: States that the priest must beware of betraying penitents' sins to others, or be deposed.
claims: A priest who reveals confessions is to be deposed.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e134.summary: Quotes Gregory: above all the priest must not tell anyone what those who confess to him have said, neither relatives nor strangers, nor, God forbid, to cause scandal; if he does, let him be deposed and wander in disgrace all his life.
claims: Revealing confessions is punished by deposition and lifelong penance.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e143.summary: Notes that the advice to choose a priest who knows how to bind and loose seems to contradict the canons that forbid anyone to judge another's parishioner.

pl-l4d21c8-d1e149.summary: Answers that it is one thing to despise one's own priest from favor or hatred, which the canons forbid, another to avoid a blind guide, which Urban advises lest the blind lead the blind. Urban: no priest may receive for penance someone committed to another priest without that priest's consent, except for the ignorance of the one first confessed to; whoever does otherwise risks his rank.
claims: Despising one's own priest is forbidden; avoiding an ignorant one is allowed.
Changing confessors requires consent, except for the first priest's ignorance.

pl-l4d21c8.summary: Teaches that as the penitent must not hide sin, which is pride, so he must not, out of humility, confess sins he knows he did not commit, since such humility is a lie that makes him a sinner, as Augustine says. Under the heading on the punishment of a priest who reveals confessions, the priest must not betray penitents' sins, on pain of deposition and lifelong wandering, as Gregory says. To the apparent conflict between choosing a priest who knows how to bind and loose and the canons forbidding judging another's parishioner, Lombard answers that despising one's own priest from favor or hatred is forbidden, but avoiding a blind guide is advised; Urban allows changing confessors only for the first priest's ignorance or with his consent.
claims: One must not confess sins one did not commit, even out of humility.
A priest who reveals confessions is to be deposed.
Avoiding an incompetent confessor is allowed; despising one's own priest is not.
Penitents may change confessors only for ignorance or with consent.
